item.title: FlyOverChina | Zunyi From Above
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
ZUNYI, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- Zunyi in southwest China's Guizhou Province has a resonant title: the "city of historic turning point." In January 1935, an enlarged meeting of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee was held in Zunyi during the Long March. The Zunyi Meeting is regarded as a crucial turning point of the Long March, leading to the ultimate success of the Chinese revolution. Since then, Zunyi has become a sacred place for generations of CPC members, and the footprints of the Red Army are forever imprinted on the city's culture and spirits. Rooted in its revolutionary past, the city is now embarking on a new chapter of development while retaining its historical significance. When the Red Army passed through, its population stood at just over 30,000. By 2025, the permanent population of its central urban area exceeded 1.6 million, with an urbanization rate of 61 percent. Zunyi also calls for developing new quality productive forces in light of local conditions and accelerating the building of a modern industrial system. The year 2026 marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. Take a drone tour above China's "city of historic turning point."

item.title: China to launch second national survey of movable cultural relics in next five years
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- China will launch its second national survey of movable cultural relics during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) to strengthen museum management and safeguard cultural heritage, a senior official said Tuesday. The survey will be part of broader efforts to improve museum governance, protect collections and promote the high-quality development of the country's museum sector, Deng Chao, deputy head of the National Cultural Heritage Administration, told a news conference. China will strengthen the inventory and documentation of collections at state-owned museums, improve the classification of cultural relics and launch a program to restore valuable items in museum collections, Deng said. The country will also refine museum management systems, strengthen professional ethics education for museum staff and encourage public oversight. Revisions to the regulations governing museums will be advanced to further standardize their operations, he said. The planned measures come amid heightened public scrutiny of museum collection management following a high-profile controversy involving the Nanjing Museum in east China's Jiangsu Province. An investigation found irregularities in the transfer and sale of five donated paintings, raising concerns about the protection and management of museum collections. Xu Huping, the museum's former head, was sentenced to three years in prison for accepting bribes. Other institutions and individuals found responsible for violations or failures in oversight were also held accountable. Deng said China would direct more resources toward the conservation of cultural relics themselves, laying a stronger foundation for the sustainable development of museums. Beyond collection protection, China will focus on improving the distribution of museums nationwide and enhancing their services, particularly at the grassroots level, during the 15th Five-Year Plan period. The number of museums in China rose from 5,788 to 7,188 during the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-2025), with the country's museums receiving a combined total of more than 6.2 billion visits, Deng said. They held 224,000 exhibitions and organized 2.25 million educational activities over the five-year period. Traveling to cities specifically to see exhibitions has repeatedly become a cultural phenomenon, while museum visits have increasingly become part of everyday life, he said. However, imbalances and shortcomings in the sector's development have also become more apparent, Deng noted. To address these challenges, China will improve planning for museum construction, promote differentiated development based on individual institutions' strengths and characteristics, and guard against redundant projects. It will also encourage the establishment of museums in suitable historic buildings and industrial heritage sites, making better use of existing heritage assets. The country will further launch an initiative to upgrade small and medium-sized museums by optimizing resource allocation and piloting support mechanisms. Under the initiative, major national and provincial museums will be encouraged to support smaller institutions through partnerships, touring exhibitions and closer cooperation. The aim is to bring high-quality exhibitions and other cultural resources to local communities while improving smaller museums' collections management, exhibitions, educational programs and professional staffing. Deng said the initiative would help smaller museums become key providers of cultural services at the grassroots level, allowing more people to enjoy high-quality exhibitions outside of major cities. ■

item.title: China establishes data-focused new central SOE to unlock data value
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
XIONGAN, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- China National Data Group Co., Ltd., a new state-owned enterprise (SOE) directly administered by the central government, was officially inaugurated at a ceremony in Xiongan New Area, north China's Hebei Province, on Tuesday. Headquartered in Xiongan New Area, the newly established enterprise is tasked with specializing in the development and utilization of data resources, bringing the total number of SOEs directly administered by the central government to 100. It is positioned as a national team for data services, a leader in data infrastructure connectivity and a strategic force for national data sci-tech innovation. The group said it will provide clients with inclusive and secure data services, and industry data governance services. Focusing on advancing China's "AI Plus" initiative, the group also vowed to provide high-quality datasets and corpora to further the development of the AI industry. The establishment of the new central SOE comes as data has increasingly become a new type of production factor driving China's digital and intelligent transformation. Unlike traditional production factors, unprocessed data can hardly generate value. Only data that is connected to real scenarios, addresses practical difficulties and undergoes processing can be transformed into usable resources, analysts said. China has been bolstering its efforts to develop a data market in recent years. In 2020, the country listed data as a new type of production factor, alongside traditional factors such as land, labor, capital and technology, highlighting its growing role in driving economic growth and digital transformation. Following the introduction of a three-year action plan in 2024 to boost the development and application of data as a production factor, China has seen the value of data resources continue to be unleashed. The plan sets out efforts to expand the breadth and depth of data applications across key sectors, foster new industries, business models and growth drivers, and unlock the multiplier effect of data in supporting high-quality development. In 2025, China's total data output reached 52.26 zettabytes, up 27.28 percent year on year and accounting for about 27.44 percent of the global total, according to a national survey on data resources released in April this year. A zettabyte is the equivalent of about one trillion gigabytes. Enterprises contributed about 90 percent of incremental data output, while emerging fields such as embodied intelligence and the low-altitude economy saw surging growth in data production, the survey noted. Traditional sectors such as industrial manufacturing, transportation and logistics, and software and information technology services also posted marked expansion in data output. To further unlock the potential of data resources, Chinese central authorities have pledged greater efforts to build an open, shared and secure nationally integrated data market, according to a set of guidelines aimed at accelerating the development of new quality productive forces. Efforts will be made to promote the deep integration of the digital economy and the real economy, and optimize the layout, construction and operation of national data infrastructure, according to the guidelines, which were jointly issued by the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the State Council earlier this month. As massive amounts of data are scattered across different departments, industries and fields, China National Data Group is expected to overcome challenges including barriers to data circulation, high data governance costs and insufficient supply of high-quality datasets, analysts said. ■

item.title: China's top economic planner vows more efforts to expand domestic demand
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- China's top economic planner said Tuesday it will work with relevant departments to expand domestic demand with greater force and more effective measures in an effort to consolidate the foundation and momentum for steady economic recovery. The National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) revealed this at a press conference on Tuesday following the release of the latest economic data on Monday, which showed the world's second-largest economy pressed ahead against pressures with a 4.6-percent economic growth in the first three quarters of 2026. Commenting on the economic performance, NDRC official Zuo Gang said the economy, in the face of intensifying global geopolitical conflicts and frequent natural disasters, has demonstrated strong resilience and vitality with new growth drivers and improved structure. Due to challenges such as the deepening impact of external shocks, an imbalance of strong supply and weak demand at home, and pronounced sectoral divergence, further measures will be taken to rev up the economy, according to the official. "The NDRC will work with relevant departments to promptly introduce and implement incremental policies and promote synergy between existing and incremental policies with a view to achieving a good start for the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030)," Zuo said. China has targeted 2026 growth at 4.5 to 5 percent and will strive for better in practice. BOOSTING CONSUMPTION More efforts will be made to vigorously boost consumption, Zuo said. Authorities will raise the share of public service spending in fiscal expenditure, strengthen inclusive policies that reach consumers directly, and promote the expansion and upgrading of goods consumption, including new energy vehicles and smart products, Zuo said. The push comes as consumption shows signs of steady improvement. Total retail sales of goods and services rose 2.6 percent year-on-year in the first three quarters of 2026, with retail sales of services growing faster than goods and new forms of consumption continuing to emerge, official data showed. Final consumption expenditure contributed more to overall economic growth in the January-September period. Chinese authorities have recently introduced a raft of measures aimed at boosting domestic demand, including offering interest subsidies for the housing loans of eligible homebuyers to help reduce home-buying costs and better unlock housing demand. Through ultra-long special treasury bond issuance, 250 billion yuan (about 37.2 billion U.S. dollars) has been raised to support consumer goods trade-in programs, and 200 billion yuan to support large-scale equipment upgrades this year. Furthermore, 50 billion yuan was earmarked for the establishment of a special fiscal-financial coordination fund to boost domestic demand. In addition to measures already announced, including lowering interest rate for pledged supplementary lending and increasing relending quotas to support sci-tech innovation and technological upgrades, "we will introduce new incremental policies in a timely manner as needed to ensure that the economy operates within an appropriate range," Zuo said. PROMOTING INVESTMENT Zuo said China will invest in both physical assets and human capital to expand effective investment. Specifically, the NDRC will push for the implementation of the 109 major projects outlined in the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) and the "six networks" initiative, covering water, power, computing, communications, urban underground pipelines and logistics networks, Zuo said. Ultra-long special treasury bond funds will be deployed more effectively, and the new policy-based financial instruments will be used at a faster pace, Zuo said, also vowing stronger support for social welfare, technology innovation, industrial upgrading and security resilience. Zuo revealed plans to energize private investment by introducing private capital into major nuclear power, hydropower, and water conservancy projects. He also identified the optimization of computing power facility layouts and the renovation and upgrading of aging reservoirs as additional investment priorities. China's investment is undergoing a profound shift in emphasis from traditional sectors to emerging ones, analysts said, noting that artificial intelligence and new infrastructure will serve as key engines for the next round of effective investment. Official data showed the country's investment in innovation-driven sectors held up well in the first three quarters of 2026, even as overall fixed-asset investment continued to contract. Investment in intellectual property products rose 9.3 percent year-on-year in the January-September period, while investment in high-tech industries grew 4.9 percent. Investment will increasingly serve the development of new quality productive forces and the building of a modern industrial system, with the ultimate results felt in expanded employment, rising incomes and improved living standards, said Liu Yuanchun, president of Shanghai University of Finance and Economics. ■

item.title: Chinese premier says SCO should promote regional stability, prosperity, contribute to global development
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
DUSHANBE, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) should strive to promote regional stability and prosperity while contributing to common development worldwide, Chinese Premier Li Qiang said here on Tuesday. Li made the remarks while addressing the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of Member States of the SCO in Tajikistan's capital of Dushanbe. Noting that this year marks the 25th anniversary of the founding of the SCO, Li said the Bishkek summit held in September achieved a series of important outcomes, injecting fresh impetus into the promotion of peace and development. Meanwhile, factors contributing to global instability and uncertainty continue to increase, he added. He noted that at the Bishkek summit, Chinese President Xi Jinping pointed out that at the crossroads concerning the future of humanity, the SCO should shoulder its historic responsibility and take the initiative in steering the course of history. To achieve this, Li said, all parties need to build greater consensus both on the level of underlying principles, including vision, philosophy and thinking, and the level of practical approaches, including operations and implementation. At the level of underlying principles, he emphasized the importance of having a clear understanding of several fundamental issues and the vision to discern broader trends. At present, Li said, different schools of thought are interacting and competing on the international stage, but multipolarity and economic globalization remain the prevailing trends. Li called for embracing a global perspective and a strong sense of responsibility for the world, saying that the SCO should continue to uphold the Shanghai Spirit. He urged the SCO to demonstrate perseverance in pursuing long-term goals. Noting that SCO countries share a common aspiration to promote friendship, safeguard security and pursue development, Li said all parties should remain steadfast, strengthen solidarity and move forward with resolve. At the level of practical approaches, the premier said all parties need to strengthen cooperation and pursue practical innovation. China stands ready to work hand in hand with all member states to enhance the organization's operational efficiency, strengthen and consolidate cooperation projects, and play a leading and exemplary role in advancing the SCO's high-quality development, implementing the four global initiatives proposed by President Xi, and building a community with a shared future for humanity, Li said. He said China is ready to work with all parties to strengthen coordination and complete, as soon as possible, the institutional frameworks and rules for the four security centers. China is also willing to sponsor 1,000 medical professionals from SCO countries to come to China for further training, continuously enhancing the well-being of people across the region, the premier said. In recent years, the international community has seen growing calls to strengthen multilateralism and reform and improve global governance, Li said, noting that the SCO should strive to unite more international partners and play an active role at the global level. To this end, he noted, it is particularly important to seek common ground while reserving differences and to build consensus while resolving differences. The SCO should strengthen economic and trade cooperation and promote regional economic integration by leveraging the complementary strengths of its members, build a stable and resilient system of international transport corridors, and safeguard the stability and smooth functioning of global industrial and supply chains, Li said. The SCO should also seek common interests amid differences in countries' concerns and work together to uphold world peace and stability, while promoting harmony and coexistence amid cultural differences, Li added. Participants said the SCO has grown steadily and gained increasing international influence since its establishment 25 years ago. They called for efforts to implement the outcomes of the Tianjin summit and Bishkek summit, further carry forward the "Shanghai Spirit," strengthen communication and coordination, promote the SCO's high-quality development and make greater contributions to regional and global peace and development. After the meeting, Li and other participating leaders of SCO member states signed and issued a joint communique and approved cooperation documents covering trade and investment, industry and connectivity, as well as resolutions concerning the SCO's development. ■

item.title: Xi congratulates Central Institute of Socialism on 70th founding anniversary
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
BEIJING, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday sent a congratulatory letter to the Central Institute of Socialism, celebrating its 70th founding anniversary. In the letter, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, praised the institute for training a large number of non-CPC representatives who share the CPC's ideals and work in unity toward common goals, and for making important contributions to consolidating and developing the patriotic united front over the past 70 years. He encouraged the institute to continue strengthening political training, building broad political consensus, and improving the quality of its teaching and research as well as its governance capacity. Xi called on the institute to play a greater role in training talent for the united front, conducting theoretical research and promoting principles and policies, so as to better serve the overall work of the CPC and the country. The congratulatory letter was read out at a gathering marking the institute's anniversary in Beijing on Tuesday. Wang Huning, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, addressed the event. Wang said Xi's congratulatory message fully recognized the institute's achievements and contributions, and set out directions and requirements for strengthening the institute and enhancing its role. Wang said the CPC Central Committee has consistently supported the development of the institute over the past 70 years. He called for stronger political consensus-building through sustained political training, higher-quality education to better train personnel for the united front, and continued efforts to enforce strict management of the institute. The institute was established on Oct. 15, 1956. Over the past seven decades, it has made significant contributions to upholding and improving the system of multiparty cooperation under the leadership of the CPC and to consolidating and strengthening the patriotic united front. ■ Wang Huning, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, addresses a gathering marking the 70th founding anniversary of the Central Institute of Socialism in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 20, 2026. Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, on Tuesday sent a congratulatory letter to the Central Institute of Socialism, celebrating its 70th founding anniversary. The congratulatory letter was read out at the gathering marking the institute's anniversary in Beijing. (Xinhua/Liu Bin)

item.title: China's Q3 economy picks up pace, reinforcing role as global growth engine
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
* China's GDP grew 4.5 percent year on year in the third quarter, higher than the second quarter's reading of 4.3 percent, supported by fast-growing new drivers and fresh policy support. * New growth drivers continued to expand, contributing more than 40 percent to China's economic growth in the first three quarters. * More foreign firms are embracing "China Opportunity 2.0," deepening their integration into China's industrial and innovation chains. BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- China's economy picked up pace in the third quarter (Q3) of 2026, supported by fast-growing new drivers and fresh policy support, staying on track to meet its annual growth target and remaining a leading engine of global growth. China's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 4.5 percent year on year in Q3, higher than the second quarter's reading of 4.3 percent, data from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) showed Monday. The world's second-largest economy generated about 107.11 trillion yuan (about 15.94 trillion U.S. dollars) in output during the January-September period, expanding 4.6 percent year on year, according to the NBS. "The national economy forged ahead against pressure and continued to shift toward innovation-driven, high-quality development, with growing positive changes in major indicators," the NBS said in a statement. China has consistently contributed around 30 percent of global economic growth, with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva saying in January that this contribution is expected to stay at roughly the same level in the coming years. GROWING RESILIENCE Noting that the GDP growth of 4.6 percent in the first three quarters is in line with the country's annual growth target, NBS deputy head Mao Shengyong told a media conference that the economy added 5.7 trillion yuan in output during the period, the largest increase for the same period in the past five years. In the third quarter, GDP growth picked up 0.2 percentage points from the second quarter, while some international institutions expected major economies to grow more slowly in July-September compared to the April-June period, Mao said. There was also a notable rise in momentum on a monthly basis. In September, value-added industrial output rose 5.5 percent year on year, 0.3 percentage points faster than in August, while the services production index gained 4.8 percent, up 0.7 percentage points from the previous month. Retail sales of consumer goods grew 1.1 percent in September, 0.7 percentage points faster than in August, and the surveyed urban unemployment rate edged down 0.1 percentage points from August to 5.2 percent. "Growth momentum showed signs of marginal improvement in September," said Wen Bin, chief economist with China Minsheng Bank, citing faster industrial and services output, a rebound in consumption and an initial stabilization of investment. China will step up efforts to expand domestic demand, improve supply, and make macro policies more effective to sustain the positive momentum of innovation-led and high-quality development, Mao said. To this end, China has recently rolled out a batch of new policies, including financial and fiscal support. "With existing policies being implemented faster and incremental policies gradually taking effect, the economy is expected to continue improving in the fourth quarter," Wen said. NEW DRIVERS AT WORK New growth drivers continued to expand, contributing more than 40 percent to China's economic growth in the first three quarters. Value-added industrial output rose 5.3 percent year on year, with equipment manufacturing up 10.2 percent and high-tech manufacturing up 14.3 percent. Output of industrial robots, lithium-ion batteries and 3D printing equipment jumped 29.1 percent, 39.5 percent and 62.5 percent, respectively. Monday's data also showed that the services sector expanded 5.2 percent year on year in the first three quarters, with information transmission, software and IT services up 10.4 percent, and leasing and business services up 12.3 percent. The shift is visible in the economic structure. Manufacturing accounted for 25.7 percent of GDP in the first three quarters, up 0.6 percentage points from a year earlier, while the share of high-tech manufacturing in the value-added output of major industrial enterprises rose 1.6 percentage points. Investment in intellectual property products climbed 9.3 percent. Traditional industries are also moving up the value chain. In Jingdezhen, a ceramics hub in east China's Jiangxi Province, local producers have embraced 3D printing in pottery making, propelling the sector's output to over 100 billion yuan. Meanwhile, some coal mining companies have implemented smart monitoring systems for underground operations, increasing efficiency by 30 percent. Green development is creating openings as well. The penetration rate of new energy vehicles in China has stayed above 60 percent for six consecutive months, while the country's energy consumption per unit of GDP fell 3.1 percent in the first three quarters. "The foundations of the economy remain solid, while new quality productive forces, modern services and high-tech foreign trade are steadily taking root," said Zhu Qigui, associate director of the China Academy of Financial Research. "As long as China continues to rely on innovation, reform and its vast market, the trend of moving toward new and better development will not change," the scholar said. SHARED OPPORTUNITIES A major trading partner of as many as 169 countries and regions, China saw its goods trade rise 18.8 percent year on year to 39.94 trillion yuan in the first three quarters. In September alone, trade grew 27.5 percent. In the first nine months, exports of mechanical and electrical products climbed 23.7 percent and accounted for 64.3 percent of total exports, while intermediate goods made up more than half of all exports, reinforcing China's role as a stabilizing anchor for global industrial and supply chains. In east China's Anhui Province, robotics manufacturer EFORT Intelligent Robot Co., Ltd. has continued to see growth in overseas orders this year, with a batch of its spraying robots set to be exported to Italy. The company's overseas revenue increased by more than 50 percent year on year in the first half of 2026. Meanwhile, the company's client, German automobile giant Volkswagen, is shifting its strategy from "in China, for China" to "in China, beyond China," with cars produced in China already exported to the Middle East and Central Asia. Foreign-invested enterprises in China remained active players in the January-September period, with their imports and exports rising 19 percent to 11.69 trillion yuan, a record high for the same period. Their trade in intermediate goods grew 27.4 percent to 7.9 trillion yuan, and their high-tech product exports jumped 42.1 percent. More foreign firms are embracing "China Opportunity 2.0," deepening their integration into China's industrial and innovation chains, Mao said. ■ (Video editors: Hong Liang and Zhu Cong)
